description: Manual ratchet wrench head: sawtooth ratchet wheel, spring-loaded pawl and hex bolt; one fixed drive direction; not a reversible, torque, impact or cordless wrench

facts.wrench: Introduce a recognizable ratchet wrench: a long handle with a red grip, a round head and one hex bolt on a fixed plate. Everything is still.
facts.cutaway: A simplified cutaway lifts the head cover to expose the toothed ratchet wheel, the spring-loaded pawl above it and the hex bolt turned by the wheel.
facts.drive: Illustrated input force swings the handle forward. The pawl sits in a gap and pushes the steep face of a tooth, so the wheel and the bolt turn together with the handle.
facts.slip: The handle swings back. The pawl rides up the sloped back of each tooth and clicks into the next gap, so the wheel and the bolt stay where they are.
facts.catch: Close-up of the forward stroke again. The spring keeps the pawl pressed into the wheel, so the pawl catches the steep face of a tooth and the wheel and bolt turn another step.
facts.repeat: The handle swings back a second time. The pawl clicks over the teeth again and the bolt keeps the extra turn. Each forward and back stroke adds one more forward turn.
facts.hold: No new part moves for this explanation. The steep face pushes the pawl and locks; the sloped face lets it slide away. The tooth shape makes the wheel turn one way only.
facts.payoff: The cover closes. Handle, pawl, wheel and bolt work together as a one-way turner. No reversing switch, motor or second tool is shown.

cue_bans.message: motion_cue must not use the word pawl; speech recognition mishears it, use wrench, ratchet, bolt or handle

narration_rules.message: only a manual one-way ratchet is depicted
